extracted.intended_audience: potential partners, clients, donors, civil society organisations, and governments interacting with the EBRD
extracted.subtask_description: High-level institutional principles and priorities that guide the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's activities, investments and partnerships across countries of operation. Emphasises transition to market economies, sustainable private sector development, core values (e.g., gender equality, integrity, environmental and social sustainability) and partnership-based implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivering prosperity via a sustainable private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Our focus is on delivering prosperity by enabling a well-run and sustainable private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBRD measures its activities by how they support prosperity through development of a healthy, sustainable private sector across its countries of operation (three continents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique business model: financing, advice and policy reform
rubrics_metrics.description: We do this with our unique business model, combining financing, advice and policy reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and interventions are expected to integrate direct finance with advisory services and where appropriate policy reform to maximise impact and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for transition to market economies
rubrics_metrics.description: The EBRD works across three continents to support the transition to successful market economies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core criterion is whether an activity contributes to the transition process (institutional and market reforms, private sector development) in countries emerging from non-market systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition (as an explicit value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary value governing EBRD work; implies priority to interventions that further political, institutional and economic transition objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Equality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named as a core value — programmes and projects should consider and promote gender equality outcomes and mainstream gender considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and compliance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrity and compliance are central standards that govern all EBRD work; projects and partners are expected to meet EBRD integrity/compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and Social Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental and social sustainability is a named value — investments should be environmentally and socially sound and sustainable, reflecting E&S safeguards and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiparty Democracy and Pluralism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBRD identifies support for multiparty democracy and pluralism as a guiding value, indicating preference for activities that uphold democratic governance and pluralistic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnering for impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBRD develops partnerships with an array of stakeholders in local and international business, investment and development communities to facilitate our work; partnership quality and alignment with EBRD objectives are important considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement (types of partners)
rubrics_metrics.description: We engage with Civil Society organisations in the countries where we work. Donors work with us to fund specific projects and initiatives. We team up with financial services providers to develop the financial sector and foster entrepreneurship and we partner with other international financial institutions such as the World Bank, joining forces in investments, strategic initiatives and policy reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBRD expects collaboration across a range of stakeholders — civil society, donors, financial service providers and other IFIs — and values partnership modalities that mobilise co-financing, technical support and policy coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional documents and legal mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement Establishing the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development was signed in Paris on 29 May 1990.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities are governed by founding and institutional documents; compliance with the Bank's mandate and governance framework is a prerequisite for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and governance / accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The EBRD is owned by 77 countries, as well as the European Union and the European Investment Bank. Each shareholder is represented on the Board of Governors, which has overall authority over the Bank. The President manages our work under the guidance of the Board of Directors. The Executive Committee and senior leadership group advise the President and oversee EBRD activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance arrangements (ownership, Board of Governors, Board of Directors, President, Executive Committee) set decision-making and accountability criteria for projects, partnerships and institutional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contactability and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting the EBRD — A-Z list of all contacts, Media enquiries, Contact a local office, Request information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bank provides clear contact channels, indicating an organisational expectation of transparency and accessibility for stakeholders seeking information or engagement.
